'''María Teresa Miras Portugal''' (19 February 1948 – 27 May 2021)<ref>[https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/ciencia/2021/05/27/fallece-maria-teresa-miras-portugal-bioquimica-ourensana-quiso-cambiar-universidad-espanola/00031622134953559231141.htm Fallece María Teresa Miras Portugal, la bioquímica ourensana que quiso cambiar la Universidad española] {{in lang|es}}</ref> was a Spanish [[scientist]], pharmacist, biochemist, molecular biologist and [[Emeritus]] [[professor]] at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]]. She was a member of the Spanish "''[[Real Academia Nacional de Farmacia]]''" and served as President of this Institution from 2007 to 2013, becoming the first woman to be elected for this position in a Spanish "[[:es:Real_Academia|Real Academia]]".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=María Teresa Miras Portugal - Real Academia de Doctores de España|url=https://www.radoctores.es/academico.php?item=26|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.radoctores.es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=María Teresa Miras-Portugal, presidenta de la Real Academia de Farmacia, defiende un cambio organizativo de la carrera|url=https://www.ibercampus.es/maria-teresa-mirasportugal-presidenta-de-la-real-academia-de-farmacia-defiende-1344.htm|access-date=2021-04-11|website=ibercampus.es|date=21 January 2007 }}</ref> She was Honorary President.<ref name=":1" /> 

She was also a member of several scientific institutions such as the Spanish Biophysical Society, the Spanish Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, the Spanish Society of Neuroscience, the [[European Society for Neurochemistry]], the [[International Society for Neurochemistry]], the Advisory Board of Chromaffin Cells, the Purinergic Club, the editorial board of the [[Journal of Neurochemistry]], the [[International Union of Basic and Clinical Pharmacology|IUPHAR]] sub-committee for the nomenclature of [[P2Y receptor|P2Y nucleotide receptors]] and the Scientific Panel of the [[NATO]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2010-01-12|title=María Teresa Miras Portugal, reelegida presidenta de la Real Academia de Farmacia|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/sociedad/2010/01/12/maria-teresa-miras-portugal-reelegida-presidenta-real-academia-farmacia/0003_8221220.htm|access-date=2021-04-11|website=La Voz de Galicia|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=CURRICULUM VITAE - Maria Teresa Miras Portugal - Enero 2018|url=https://www.ranf.com/wp-content/uploads/academicos/documentacion/numero/miras2018_cv.pdf%7Caccess-date=2021-04-11%7Clanguage=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=María Teresa Miras, elegida "Gallega de Abril" por el Grupo Correo Gallego|url=https://www.elcorreogallego.es/especiales/gallegos-premiados/gallegos-premiados-2007/maria-teresa-miras-elegida-gallega-abril-grupo-correo-gallego-HDCG161457|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.elcorreogallego.es|date=30 April 2007 |language=es-ES}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Miras Portugal, Mª Teresa – Real Academia Nacional de Farmacia|url=https://www.ranf.com/academico/miras-portugal-ma-teresa/|access-date=2021-04-11|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Mª Teresa Miras reelegida Presidente – Real Academia Nacional de Farmacia|url=https://www.ranf.com/noticia/ma-teresa-miras-reelegida-presidente/|access-date=2021-04-11|language=es}}</ref>

== Biography ==
María Teresa Miras Portugal was born in 1948 in [[O Carballiño]] ([[Province of Ourense|Orense]]), where she completed her primary and secondary studies. She started her university studies in Pharmacy in the [[University of Santiago de Compostela]] and continued them at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]]. Her marks at the [[Licentiate (degree)|Licenciate]] university degree led her to get a Special Mention at National Level.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Alejandra|title=Marzo 2021: Mª Teresa Miras Portugal|url=https://www.sebbm.es/web/es/divulgacion/mujeres-ciencia/retratos/4452-marzo-m-teresa-miras-portugal|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.sebbm.es|language=en-gb|archive-date=12 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210412120733/https://www.sebbm.es/web/es/divulgacion/mujeres-ciencia/retratos/4452-marzo-m-teresa-miras-portugal|url-status=dead}}</ref> She completed a PhD in Sciences at the [[University of Strasbourg]] and Pharmacy at the Complutense University of Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web|title=madri+d. Entrevista a: Mª Teresa Miras-Portugal|url=http://www.madrimasd.org/cienciaysociedad/entrevistas/revista-madrimasd/detalleEmpresa.asp?id=500|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.madrimasd.org}}</ref> She later became a professor of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology at the [[University of Oviedo]], the [[University of Murcia]] and the Complutense University of Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miras Portugal, Mª Teresa – Real Academia Nacional de Farmacia|url=https://www.ranf.com/academico/miras-portugal-ma-teresa/|access-date=2021-04-11|language=es}}</ref>

In her more than 40 years engaged in research, she focused in the study of nucleotide receptors and their impact on neurodegenerative diseases<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Tribuna Complutense :: UCM|url=https://www.ucm.es/tribunacomplutense/61/art984.php#.YHNETuhKjIU|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.ucm.es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title= madri+d. Entrevista a: Mª Teresa Miras-Portugal|url=http://www.madrimasd.org/cienciaysociedad/entrevistas/revista-madrimasd/detalleEmpresa.asp?id=500|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.madrimasd.org}}</ref> and published more than 350 research articles in specialized journals,<ref name=":0" /> combining this research with teaching and institutional work. In 2012, she was appointed president of the Committee of Experts for the study of the need for reforms in the Spanish university system.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=MARÍA TERESA MIRAS PORTUGAL Catedrática de Bioquímica y Biología Molecular de la UCM {{!}} Revista de la Sociedad Española de Bioquímia y Biología Molecular {{!}} SEEBM|url=https://www.sebbm.es/revista/articulo.php?id=198&url=mara-teresa-miras-portugal-catedratica-de-bioquimica-y-biologia-molecular-de-la-ucm|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.sebbm.es}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2005 she received the Alberto Sols Medal to Research in Biochemistry,<ref name=":1" /> in 2008 the María Josefa Wonenburger Planells Prize by the Xunta de Galicia,<ref>{{Cite web|title=María Teresa Miras Portugal {{!}} Unidade Muller e Ciencia|url=https://unidadedamullereciencia.xunta.gal/es/premio-maria-josefa-wonenburger/maria-teresa-miras-portugal|access-date=2021-04-11|website=unidadedamullereciencia.xunta.gal}}</ref> in 2011 the Community of Madrid honoured her with the Miguel Catalán Research Award for her entire professional career<ref name=":2" /> and in 2016 in Galicia received the Castelao Medal.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lugo|first=El Progreso de|date=2016-06-18|title=Alfredo Conde, Xerardo Estévez, Teresa Miras, Xosé Antonio Vilaboa y Cántigas, distinguidos|url=https://www.elprogreso.es/articulo/galicia/medallas-castelao-2016-cantigas-da-terra-alfredo-conde-xerardo-estevez-teresa-miras-y/20160618133342378400.html|access-date=2021-04-11|website=El Progreso de Lugo|language=es}}</ref>

She was given [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorates]] from the [[University of Murcia]] and the [[King Juan Carlos University]] and was an honorific member of the Academia Nacional de Farmacia y Bioquímica de Argentina, Académie Nationale de Pharmacie de France, Académie Européenne des Sciences des Arts et des Lettres and the [[Academia Europaea|European Academy]] (physiology and medicine).<ref name=":0" />
